These sum to (1). The monotonicity in gap follows by subtraction, strict increase in k by convex interpolation of the near and far endpoints. A regular bipartite double count shows uniformity of the fixed-point-pairing map, and direct pair comparison gives the positive odd inversion increment. The independent finite checker replayed 675381 exact assertions; infinite claims follow from proofs, not finite enumeration. Degenerate endpoints and n=2 are handled.

originality.rationale: The local gap-resolved pair inversion probability and uniform class-to-class coupling are compared by mathematical implication against full-text primary literature. Désarménien/Dukes/Hart–Rowley cover the fixed-point-refined generating polynomial for total inversion count, which subsumes the conditional mean but does not resolve individual position pairs. Pinsky and Pinsky–Schickentanz give local inversion probabilities for different measures on all permutations, not involution conjugacy classes. Hansson gives Bruhat gradedness, not the uniform coupling. The inspected published comparisons do not contain the target law. Residual older-priority risk remains.

value.rationale: The precise index-gap probability is a canonical local statistic in permutation ranking models and resolves spatial information discarded by previously known total-inversion enumerators. Its strict spatial slope and exact full-matching flatness boundary are structural. The matching-growth coupling yields a strictly ordered sequence of full inversion-count laws, not only a moment comparison, and a nontrivial macroscopic spatial profile. This is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of a known count table.
